messages:
Alex K: evening handoff — quick summary:
Alex K: primary for the shift is Samir, secondary is Maria L. I'm handing over an active incident (KV/prefix cache pressure causing tail latency + intermittent 429s for some tenants).
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT created: #INC-5723 — "KV cache pressure leading to 429s". Pager routed to @Samir and @Maria L at 2026-03-14T17:07:14Z.
Alex K: impact: ~4 tenants hit intermittent 429s (mostly writes). Traffic dropped automatically due to request-level retries. No data loss reported. Support tickets opened for the 3 largest customers.
Samir: ack. I've seen the graphs — 95th/99th token latency spiked after the kernel patch + new batching window. Current mitigation: rolled back kernel patch on 3/4 nodes, scaled dedicated pool +2 GPUs (temporary), and enabled aggressive prefix caching.
Maria L: backing Samir. After rollback we saw reduced tail latency but a small memory pressure signal persists on rtx-backend-7. I'm running heap checks and kv-cache metrics now.
Devon: customer-facing note: support updated customers A, B, and C. Estimated impacted requests ~0.3% of global QPS, most succeeded on retry. Flagged for SRE postmortem if root cause confirmed as runtime leak.
Samir: runbook pointers: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-pressure (see section "rollback-and-scale") and ops playbook https://redwood.internal/ops/playbooks/cpu-mem-leak. Commands I ran:
Samir: ```
# rollback kernel patch
kubectl -n inference set image ds/runtime runtime:v2026-03-12
# scale pool
redwoodctl pool set-size dedicated-gpu-pool 12
``` 
Alex K: logs saved to /var/log/incidents/INC-5723 and longterm traces forwarded to tracing-service (link in runbook).
Oncall Bot: Note: auto-fallback activated to smaller model variant for tiered customers at 17:09Z — this reduced per-token latency but increased token cost by ~4% for those requests.
Maria L: intermediate status: system stable but degraded. Alerts for 429 rate reduced after scale + rollback. Still seeing occasional 500s from rtx-backend-7 under burst. I'll keep a cron job to scrape heap and trigger a restart if RSS > 70% for 15m.
Samir: next steps (overnight): 1) Maria to monitor rtx-backend-7 and trigger restart if threshold hits; 2) I will run a targeted memory profiler on the canary node at 02:00 UTC; 3) Alex to coordinate support and draft customer comms if we need scheduled restarts.
Alex K: coverage note: I have a calendar conflict 02:00–04:00 UTC. Maria, can you cover the profiler run if it needs manual intervention? If not, we need to swap with Ops Rotations.
Maria L: I can cover 02:00–03:00 but blocked 03:00–04:00 for infra patch window. Ops Rotations, can you pick up 03:00–04:00 please?
Ops Rotations: we can cover 03:00–04:30 if needed. @Devon will be primary contact for customer comms during that window.
Devon: roger. I'll keep the customer comms draft updated in the incident doc and monitor support channel. If we decide on rolling restarts (non-emergency), schedule should be 04:15–04:45 UTC to minimize overlap with APAC peak.
Alex K: handoff checklist completed: logs + runbook links in doc, mitigation done (rollback + scale + prefix cache), owners assigned (Samir primary, Maria secondary). I'll be offline from 18:30Z+. Samir, any final notes?
Samir: nothing else. I'll post a one-line status update every hour in this thread. If anything escalates, page both primary and secondary. Good handoff, thanks.
Maria L: thanks all, leaving monitoring hooks and alerts on. Good luck overnight. :thumbsup:
Devon: signed, will be watching support. We'll regroup morning shift and start RCA.
Alex K: handing off — over and out.
